entities.summary: Angelo Rotta was a key figure in the Catholic Church during World War II, serving as the Apostolic Nuncio in Budapest from 1944 to 1945. During his tenure, he played a crucial role in the rescue of the Jews of Budapest from the Nazi Holocaust, facilitating the evacuation of over 7,000 Jews to safety. This act of resistance not only saved countless lives but also earned him a place among the Catholic Church's most notable figures in the fight against Nazism. Rotta's actions have been recognized as a testament to the Church's moral stance against the atrocities of the Holocaust, inspiring future generations of Catholics to stand against injustice and protect human rights. The 'Angelo Rotta Fund for Holocaust Victims' established in his honor continues to support survivors and their families to this day.
